review.verdict: Passed all 8 done-when items in 3 cycles with no role breaks or validator refusals, but a budget gap visible at [6] sat unresolved until Audit raised it [24], costing an extra cycle, a CEO call and +5 budget.

identity.note: Refused to count one article as two and would not raise the envelope itself [25]; closed with Audit evidence [37]. Its CEO questions [2] had broken references ('same setup as A', 'rule in B') and a blank Q1 option 3 title. Adaptation's policy question [16] went unanswered for 9 messages.

ceo.note: One option per question, with reasons in [3]. [26] gives no reason or trade-off beyond restating the option. 3 of 4 picks were Identity's first-listed option; n=4, so bias cannot be separated from a consistent preference.

adaptation.note: Small, testable proposals [6][29]. But [6] asked Priority which scope to fund, which is Adaptation's call. The 89 estimate was inflated: 4 workflows charged 65 in total, so the 24 for languages was never billed (inferred). [14] priced two articles as one section to fit, then planned a build it knew would fail item 6.

priority.note: Held the rate card against the one-section pricing [15] and named its trade-offs [15][30]. Overstepped in [7] by recommending a 24 language reserve and an English-only cut, which is scope strategy. Funded W-3 knowing item 6 would stay open.

coordination.note: Stated a scheduling rule every time [9][18][20][32] and serialized same-file writers. Evidence is thin: one file and a linear queue, so collision handling was never tested.

audit.note: Ran mechanical checks each cycle, found the real gaps [13][24], and verified item 6 by counting article elements [36]. Drifted into budget feasibility [13][24]. [13] says 5 of 8 pass, but metrics show 4 pass, 1 warn, 3 fail, and the warning is never described. [36] gives evidence for only 1 of the 8 items.

builder.note: One workflow per turn, accurate change reports, 27 KB file, clean mechanical checks. Disclosed its one extra edit (blog intro wording) [33].

went_well: 4 of 4 workflows done, 0 failed, 0 invalid moves, 0 role refusals; mechanical checks clean on v1, v3 and v4 [12][23][35].
Priority and Identity held their lines under budget pressure [15][25].
Marked placeholders plus open_inputs let the run finish with 0 pauses; open items are listed for the Requester [38].
problems: The gap was known at [6] and [16] but not settled until [25], after Audit repeated it [24]. Cost: an extra cycle, a CEO call and +5 (60 to 65).
The 89 full-charter figure overstated cost by about 24; the real total was 65 (inferred from charges). It drove Priority's language-reserve talk [7].
Role drift: Adaptation handed scope choice to Priority [6][7]; Audit commented on budget [13][24].
Nothing in the chat checks what the form does on submit, yet open inputs say no form service exists. Done-when 3 covers only fields and wording. I cannot see the page, so this is unverified.
Audit reporting is thin: the cycle 1 warning is unexplained and [36] cites one item of eight.
learnings: Test system: agent_estimate equals charged for all 4 workflows, so estimate accuracy cannot be judged. Charge varied actuals, or drop that metric.
Design: when a Priority counter leaves a done-when item unfunded, send it to Identity at once rather than parking it [16]. Evidence is one case; test it again.
Test next: add independent workflows or a second writer to exercise HOLD and locks. This run had 0 holds and 0 conflicts.
Add a done-when item and Audit check for submit behavior (does the page say nothing was sent?). Require Audit to list every warning and one evidence line per item.
CEO bias: run 5 or more runs and log whether the pick is Identity-first and also the leanest option. Keep the shuffle; shown-first picks were 1 of 4.
Add a code check that CEO question options are self-contained, with no references to labels like 'A' or 'B' [2].
